report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 3 of cancel.py: WindowsJobBackend, PosixSessionBackend, select_backend, live registry, ManagedProcess class with init, properties, cancel method.

handoff.purpose: Implement Windows and POSIX process containment backends, live process registry, and ManagedProcess class with cancellation logic.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.after_spawn
symbols.note: Assigns process to Windows job object and resumes all threads.

symbols.name: WindowsJobBackend.kill_tree
symbols.note: Terminates job object or kills process if no job.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend
symbols.note: Contains process tree via session/process group.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend._pgid
symbols.note: Returns process group ID, falling back to PID.

symbols.name: PosixSessionBackend.kill_tree
symbols.note: Sends SIGKILL to process group, falls back to process.kill().

symbols.name: select_backend
symbols.note: Returns WindowsJobBackend for win platforms, else PosixSessionBackend.

symbols.name: live_managed_processes
symbols.note: Returns list of ManagedProcesses with returncode None.

symbols.name: cancel_all_managed
symbols.note: Cancels every live ManagedProcess, returns CancelResult list.

symbols.name: ManagedProcess
symbols.note: Wraps a subprocess with cancellation support.

symbols.name: ManagedProcess.__init__
symbols.note: Spawns process, sets up containment, registers in _LIVE.

symbols.name: ManagedProcess.cancel
symbols.note: Signals group, waits grace, then kills tree.

claims.text: Only now is it safe to let the child run: anything it spawns from here on is born inside the job.
claims.why: The comment explains the timing of resuming threads, but the property that spawned children are inside the job depends on Windows behavior not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE: closing the last handle destroys any survivor.
claims.why: The comment refers to Windows job object flag KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, which is not set in this chunk; the effect depends on code outside the chunk.

claims.text: Contain the tree in its own session/process group.
claims.why: The class uses start_new_session=True in popen_kwargs, and signal_group/kill_tree use os.killpg, which operates on process groups.

claims.text: Pick the containment backend for a platform string (sys.platform). Split out as a pure function so the platform decision is assertable from either OS without spawning anything.
claims.why: The function returns a class based on platform.startswith('win'), no side effects.

claims.text: The cancel token reaches a child only if every layer between the loop driver and the spawn remembered to thread it through. The kill switch may not depend on that: a driver that forgot one cancel= argument would leave a pytest tree or a vendor CLI running after the operator pulled the plug, and 'the loop stopped but its children did not' is not stopping. This is the sweep of last resort -- KillSwitch.stop_children calls it on every trip.
claims.why: The comment references KillSwitch.stop_children from another module, not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A WeakSet, so registration cannot keep a finished process object alive and cannot leak; entries are also discarded eagerly on close().
claims.why: _LIVE is a weakref.WeakSet; weak references allow garbage collection of unreferenced ManagedProcess objects.

claims.text: Snapshot of every contained child alive in THIS interpreter.
claims.why: Function returns list of processes with returncode None (alive) from _LIVE WeakSet.

claims.text: Never raises: one wedged child must not stop the rest from being killed. The default grace is 0.0, not DEFAULT_GRACE_S -- this is the emergency path, where the whole point is to be fast, and a child that would have exited politely within three seconds is no less dead for being killed now.
claims.why: Function catches Exception per child and continues; default grace_s=0.0 is used (not DEFAULT_GRACE_S).

claims.text: Use as a context manager; leaving the block cancels anything still running and then releases the container. Dropping the last reference also releases the container, which on win32 kills any survivor -- an orphaned ManagedProcess must not leave writers behind.
claims.why: Context manager behavior (__enter__/__exit__) is not present in this chunk; release on last reference relies on __del__ not shown.

claims.text: Registered ONLY here: after containment is established. A process we failed to contain is killed above and must never appear in a registry that promises 'cancelling this reaps its tree'.
claims.why: The code registers in _LIVE only after successful after_spawn; on failure, process is killed and release called.

claims.text: Idempotent: cancelling an already-exited process is a no-op that reports already_exited.
claims.why: If process.poll() is not None, returns CancelResult with STAGE_ALREADY_EXITED immediately.

observations.what: WindowsJobBackend.after_spawn resumes all threads after assigning to job, ensuring spawned children are in job.
PosixSessionBackend uses start_new_session and killpg for process group containment.
Live registry uses WeakSet and thread lock for safe concurrent access.
ManagedProcess.__init__ handles failures by killing process and releasing backend.
cancel_all_managed catches all exceptions per process to avoid blocking.
ManagedProcess.cancel uses grace_s parameter, defaults to DEFAULT_GRACE_S.
